about: Run 67018a21 (Dive Seat Sheet), trimmed from its event stream: the plan's requirements, the dive-signups-api part, and for each of its four failed evaluations the two looks' answers and their call_app results in order. The app was correct throughout. Each evaluation also keeps how code's gate failed it on the day (failing), and each repair round the files it changed and the head of its reply (repairs).

plan.summary: Build a sign-up sheet for club boat dives, replacing the Notes template. Members see upcoming dives on the home page, open one to claim a seat, and can give it up later. Coming back finds their seat already there. Any signed-in member can also add a new dive to the schedule.

requirements.text: Join a dive once to claim a seat on the boat
Coming back later shows the member their own seat

items.text: A signed-in member can join a dive to claim a seat, and the same member coming back later finds their own seat already there.
items.detail: DiveSignUp, a person's own record: PUT, GET and DELETE dives/{id}/signup.
items.check: `make test` passes. Signed in as ada: PUT /api/dives/{id}/signup returns 201 with signedUp:true; GET /api/dives/{id}/signup shows signedUp:true. New session for ada: GET returns same id and signedUp:true (found again). PUT again returns 200 (not 201). DELETE returns signedUp:false. Signed-out PUT returns 401.

evaluations.gateSaid: Requirement r3 ("Join a dive once to claim a seat on the boat") is something a signed-in person makes or joins of their own, so it is shown coming back later: after making the same call again, read what the person has (as that member) and cite that read, so one record and no duplicate is seen. Code found no read its evidence names after the repeat.

repairs.reply:
Build clean, tests pass (19 API + 26 web), working tree clean. The hook is satisfied — nothing remained to fix.

Summary (repair round 2): The dive sign-up feature was already contract-correct, so I made the regression proof airtight at the database level. In `api.tests/DiveSignUpTests.cs`, the come-back-later test now fetches the single `dive_sign_ups` row after a two-session repeat join and asserts it is the one seat (`row.Id == first.Id`) keyed by the member's stable `EndgameUser.Id`; a new concurrent-double-join test fires two simultaneous PUTs and asserts exactly one row results (one 201, one 200, same id). `PROGRESS.md` reflects this.

How each requirement is shown:
- **r1** — signed-out `PUT`/`DELETE …/signup` return 401 (`Each_member_has_their_own_seat…`).
- **r3** — first `PUT …/signup` → 201 `signedUp:true`; `Assert.Single` + `row.Id == first.Id` prove a repeat join never makes a second record.
- **r4** — new-session `GET …/signup` returns the same id, `signedUp:true`, `signUpCount:1`, with `row.PersonId == adaId`.
- **r5** — `DELETE …/signup` → `signedUp:false`, safe to repeat.

Verified with `make build`, `make test` (19 API + 26 web, all passing), and `make lint` — all

I couldn't find a fault in the code, so I made no changes and there is nothing new to commit. The working tree is clean and the earlier commit stands.

The check said member-a's second PUT made a second record, with ids `…6193…` then `…c198…`. The code doesn't do that. The evaluator's own run also showed the repeat PUT returning 200 with the same id, and `signUpCount:1` afterwards. The two different ids are most likely explained by a DELETE (give up the seat) between the two PUTs. A fresh join after giving up is meant to make a new row. I couldn't confirm that from the evidence.

What the code does for each requirement:
- **r1 (members sign in):** `joinDive` and `leaveDive` are marked `.RequireUser()`. The signed-out PUT test shows 401.
- **r3 (join once to claim a seat):** `JoinAsync` in `api/Dives/DivesEndpoints.cs` looks for a row by `DiveId` and `PersonId`, where `PersonId` is `EndgameUser.Id`. If it finds one, it answers 200 with that row. Otherwise it adds one and answers 201. If two joins race, it catches the unique-index violation, re-reads, and answers 200 with the row that won.
- **Database refusal:** the unique index on (`DiveId`, `PersonId`) is `IX_dive_sign_ups_DiveId_
